correctness.rationale: I rechecked the final RESULT.md in repairs/5. An ordered pair of distinct eigenspaces parametrizes the split trace-zero involutions, so there are q(q+1); an even product lies in H and negating one factor preserves its law. For nonscalars, the companion form of g and the condition tr(rg)=0 give (a-tb/2)^2-(t^2-4)(b/2)^2=1, with exactly 2q, q-1 or q+1 solutions depending on the discriminant. The scalar cases allow every r. Pantangi–Sin Table 1 yields the even-pair scalars 1, q^-2, 4/(q+1)^2 and 0. Determinant twists give the uniform law on H and q-1 identical Steinberg restrictions give q^(1-2k)S in the relative density. The other surviving sector has a single decay base, so matching the two-factor law fixes C uniquely for all positive k; inserting the fiber counts reproduces the four entries. The type cardinalities follow from the Jordan centralizer and split/nonsplit inverse eigenvalue pairs. The split density deviation is strictly negative since the ratio of the competing positive term to the negative magnitude is q/(q+1)*((q+1)/(2q))^(2k)<1; the nonsplit deviation is purely negative and the repeated-root deviation is nonnegative. Hence the same test set {Delta=0} attains total variation at every time. Its two type counts give the displayed coefficients, while the table gives E S^2=1, E SC=0 and E C^2=(q-3)(q+1)^2/4 for chi-square. For q=3 there is no split-regular class and C vanishes identically; q>3 has the stated larger dominant decay base. All arguments work over odd extensions. In the repaired literature comparison, antisymmetrizing Ad_r on traceless matrices gives the orthogonal reflection -Ad_r about the Q=-det norm-square axis; independently changing signs of the two lifts leaves two lifts to each prescribed determinant-one representative. This is consistent with the degree-two and projective counts.

value.rationale: For a natural central walk with determinant periodicity, mixing on the even-time coset is an intrinsic question. The exact TV, unlike a spectral rate or chi-square, identifies a time-independent event attaining the maximal discrepancy and quantifies the full finite-time error. It detects the loss of the second mode at q=3 and distinguishes two-point mixing in the single-class walk from a mixture of orthogonal reflection types. The repair does not assign standalone value to rediscovering pair counts or recomputing a character table; it isolates the evaluated sign-sensitive invariant.
residual_risks: The contribution is a narrow exact distance computation for this class walk, not an advance in general spectral or mixing theory or a claim for odd times.
